permit.exempt_list_quote: [A] 105.2 Work Exempt From Permit. Exemptions from permit requirements of this code shall not be deemed to grant authorization for any work to be done in any manner in violation of the provisions of this code. Permits shall not be required for the following: Gas: Portable heating appliance. Replacement of any minor part that does not alter approval of equipment or make such equipment unsafe. Mechanical: Portable heating appliance. Portable ventilation equipment. Portable cooling unit. Steam, hot or chilled water piping within any heating or cooling equipment regulated by this code. Replacement of any part that does not alter its approval or make it unsafe. Portable evaporative cooler. Self-contained refrigeration system containing 10 pounds (4.54 kg) or less of refrigerant and actuated by motors of 1 horsepower (0.75 kW) or less. The installation, replacement, removal or metering of any load management control device. Plumbing: The stopping of leaks in drains, water, soil, waste or vent pipe [...] The clearing of stoppages or the repairing of leaks in pipes, valves or fixtures and the removal and reinstallation of water closets, provided such repairs do not involve or require the replacement or rearrangement of valves, pipes or fixtures. [...] [A] 105.2.2 Minor Repairs. Ordinary minor repairs may be made with the approval of the building official without a permit, provided the repairs do not include the cutting away of any wall, partition or portion thereof, the removal or cutting of any structural beam or load-bearing support, or the removal or change of any required means of egress [...]
permit.source_note: This is the Florida Building Code, Building, 8th Edition (2023), Section 105.2, read on a secondary copy (UpCodes). Orlando publishes no list of its own for commercial work on orlando.gov; any city change to it would be in Orlando City Code Chapter 13, which could not be opened on Municode (403). The city's interactive permit guide (digitalpermits.orlando.gov, 'Figure Out What Permits You Need') is a web application and was not used.
permit.note: The state list covers only minor gas, mechanical and plumbing items. Toilet partitions or compartments are not named. 'Partition' appears only in the minor-repairs clause, in the sense of a wall. Orlando's 'Get a Permit' page says: 'By law, the State of Florida requires you to get a permit for most projects, even small ones.' The city's only published dollar exemption is the state's residential one (single-family dwellings, work under $7,500, from July 1, 2026), which does not apply to commercial restrooms.
permit.second_quote: By law, the State of Florida requires you to get a permit for most projects, even small ones.
permit.third_quote: Effective July 1, 2026, a new state law (HB803) exempts owners and contractors of single-family dwellings from the requirement to obtain a building permit for work valued at less than $7,500, when exemption eligibility requirements are met.
permit.office: City of Orlando Permitting Services Division

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Orlando job sites. Price your restroom, pick a material for Florida humidity and see the rules that apply.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Orlando hotels, attractions, schools and offices, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** Florida's plumbing rules set the number of toilets and urinals by how many people use the building, and Orlando applies them unchanged. The table below shows what that means.
page.code_change_bullet: - **New rules on December 31, 2026:** Florida replaces its building rules with a new edition that day. Orlando reviews permit applications submitted on or before December 30, 2026 under the current rules, and applications submitted from December 31 under the new ones.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** Orlando says Florida law requires a permit for most projects, even small ones. The building rules' list of work that needs no permit covers minor gas, mechanical and plumbing repairs, and doesn't name toilet partitions. Ask Orlando Permitting Services whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.stalls_after: In restaurants and other gathering places, Florida can require three women's toilets for every two men's toilets and urinals once the men's room has more than two. Licensed restaurants may be exempt, so confirm with Orlando Permitting Services. Outdoor seating counts toward the number of people. At least one stall in each room must be wheelchair accessible.
page.capacity: To find your building's capacity, the building rules count an office at one person per 150 square feet of floor, a restaurant dining room at one per 15 square feet and a classroom at one per 20. Your architect or Orlando Permitting Services sets the final number.
page.install_rule: Contractors who get permits in Orlando register with the city's Permitting Services Division first, with a business tax receipt, their state certification and proof of workers' compensation cover. Florida has no state license category specifically for toilet partitions, and a contractor whose work falls in a licensed category needs that license, so confirm with Orlando Permitting Services which one covers your job. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: A contractor who gets a permit in Orlando registers with the city's Permitting Services Division first.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** Florida has no state wage law for public construction and doesn't let cities or school districts set one. On federally funded work the federal rate applies: $28.65 an hour plus $13.80 in benefits for a carpenter on building work in Orange County.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 6.5% in Orlando: 6% state and 0.5% Orange County. The county's 0.5% applies only to the first $5,000 of each item.
page.buyers_extra: - **Hotels, attractions and convention venues:** HDPE or phenolic where crowds are heavy and stalls are washed down every night, and finishes that match the property in guest-facing restrooms.

Orlando City Code, Chapter 13 (Building Code), which holds the city's administrative amendments, could not be opened on [Municode](https://library.municode.com/fl/orlando/codes/code_of_ordinances?nodeId=TITIICICO_CH13BUCO). - Sales tax in Orange County: Florida Department of Revenue, [Form DR-15DSS, Discretionary Sales Surtax Information for Calendar Year 2026](https://floridarevenue.com/Forms_library/current/dr15dss_26.pdf) (Orange County 0.5%, in effect since January 1, 2003), [Discretionary Sales Surtax](https://floridarevenue.com/taxes/taxesfees/Pages/discretionary.aspx) for the $5,000 limit, and the [Tax Information Publications list](https://floridarevenue.com/taxes/tips/Pages/default.aspx), which carries no notice of a change for Orange County. Checked 2026-11-24.

page.official_names: - The rules by their official names: 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design; Florida Building Code, 8th Edition (2023): Building, Plumbing and Accessibility volumes, in force since December 31, 2023 and applied in Orlando to permit applications submitted on or before December 30, 2026; replaced by the 9th Edition (2026) for applications submitted on or after December 31, 2026; Florida Building Code, Building, Section 105.2 for work exempt from permits; Orlando City Code, Chapter 13 (Building Code); NFPA 286 for HDPE under the International Building Code, the model for Florida's code.
